question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(160,0.55),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X\le 95).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8577\,$ | $\,0.8599\,$ | $\,0.8621\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ | $\,0.8810\,$ | $\,0.8830\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ | $\,0.8997\,$ | $\,0.9015\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=160$ and $p=0.55.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =160\cdot 0.55 \\  & =88 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =160\cdot (1-0.55) \\  & =72 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(160)(0.55)=88
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(160)(0.55)(1-0.55)=39.6.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(88,39.6).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X\le 95).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X\le 95)≈P(Y\le 95.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 95.5) & =P(Z\le \frac{95.5-88}{\sqrt{39.6}}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le 1.19) \\  & =Φ(1.19) \\  & =0.883\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X\le 95)≈0.883.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.8836.$
